package_info.package_versions: All versions where Trace.axd is enabled in production
package_info.why_malicious: When enabled in production, Trace.axd exposes sensitive diagnostic and session data, including plaintext credentials, session tokens, and internal application state, to unauthenticated users. This creates a critical information disclosure vulnerability.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Trace.axd handler outputs recent web request logs, including session state, application state, request/response cookies, and HTTP headers, to any user accessing the endpoint.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C# (ASP.NET built-in feature, not user code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Trace.axd handler collects and displays detailed diagnostic information for the last 80 web requests, including session variables, cookies, HTTP headers, and potentially POST body data, to any unauthenticated user accessing the endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exposing internal diagnostic and session data to unauthenticated users is a critical security risk, as it can reveal credentials, session tokens, and other sensitive information.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to restrict Trace.axd to authenticated administrators or disable it entirely in production. Actual behavior allows public, unauthenticated access.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Trace.axd is legitimately used in development environments for debugging and diagnostics, but should never be exposed in production.
key_indicators: Displays session state, including plaintext credentials
Shows request/response cookies and HTTP headers
Reveals physical directory structure and internal application state

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers the /Trace.axd endpoint is publicly accessible on the target ASP.NET application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker views recent web requests and diagnostic data.

attack_chain.action: Attacker inspects trace logs for sensitive information such as usernames, passwords, session tokens, and internal application state.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains credentials or session tokens.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses exposed credentials or session tokens to impersonate users or escalate privileges within the application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential account takeover or further compromise of the application.

behavioral_signatures: Trace.axd responses containing session state, application state, or POST body data
Repeated unauthenticated access to Trace.axd from external IPs
file_indicators: Trace.axd endpoint present and accessible in production
network_indicators: HTTP GET/POST requests to /Trace.axd from untrusted or external sources
Large responses from /Trace.axd containing diagnostic data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for public access to /Trace.axd endpoints in production environments. Scan web applications for the presence of Trace.axd and verify that it is not accessible without authentication. Review web.config files for trace enabled="true" settings. Alert on responses from Trace.axd that include session state, credentials, or other sensitive data.
